players.product: Optical amplifiers (EDFA) for data center interconnect (DCI), incl. pluggable SFP+ EDFA and ultra-compact single-channel amplifiers

quarterly_data.signal: H1 2026 half-year report (DART, separate financials): H1 revenue KRW 7,229,274,364 (H1 2025: KRW 6,307,651,349); H1 operating loss KRW 746,523,264 (H1 2025: loss KRW 1,525,919,881); H1 net loss KRW 598,327,003. Q2 alone: revenue KRW 4,530,334,520 (Q2 2025: KRW 2,542,965,156) and operating profit KRW 128,132,378 (Q2 2025: operating loss KRW 1,063,954,802). Product revenue by line (KRW thousand): optical amplifiers 4,795,542 (H1 2025: 4,626,406), optical transceivers 411,571 (961,202), optical repeater (DAS) modules 1,909,419 (331,917), fiber lasers 51,398 plus 52,764 merchandise. Revenue by region (KRW thousand): Japan 3,949,487 (3,538,169), Europe and other 961,382 (1,157,072), Korea 2,318,405 (1,612,410).
quarterly_data.figure: H1 revenue KRW 7,229,274,364 (H1 2025 KRW 6,307,651,349); Q2 revenue KRW 4,530,334,520, Q2 OP KRW 128,132,378; optical amplifier revenue KRW 4,795,542 thousand

quarterly_data.signal: Single sales / supply contracts disclosed in the report: two contracts for optical amplifiers used in data center interconnect (DCI) with 1Finity - KRW 3,868,513,903 (reported 2026.06.04, term 2026.06.02 to 2027.12.06) and KRW 2,071,253,765 (reported 2026.06.09, term 2026.06.08 to 2028.02.21); revenue to be recognised sequentially after the customer's delivery schedule and acceptance. Order backlog at the end of H1 2026: KRW 19,115 million in total, of which optical amplifiers 14,494 units / KRW 14,686 million (orders received 17,824 units / KRW 19,481 million, delivered 3,330 units / KRW 4,796 million), fiber lasers KRW 2,640 million, optical repeaters KRW 1,398 million, optical transceivers KRW 391 million.
quarterly_data.figure: DCI amplifier contracts with 1Finity KRW 3,868,513,903 and KRW 2,071,253,765; order backlog KRW 19,115 million (optical amplifiers KRW 14,686 million)

quarterly_data.signal: Production capacity and utilisation in H1 2026 (value basis, KRW million): optical amplifiers capacity 4,302, production 2,198, utilisation 51.1%; optical transceivers capacity 1,240, production 377, utilisation 30.4%; optical repeaters capacity 1,566, production 1,288, utilisation 82.3%. No investment plan was confirmed at the half-year end, but the company was reviewing capacity (CAPA) expansion and capex for optical amplifiers for AI data centers and fiber lasers for defense; the funds raised in July 2026 are to be invested in new production lines and equipment expansion from 2027 to 2028.
quarterly_data.figure: Optical amplifier utilisation 51.1% (capacity KRW 4,302 million, production KRW 2,198 million); repeaters 82.3%; transceivers 30.4%; new lines 2027 to 2028

quarterly_data.signal: Company statements in the report: its pluggable (plug-and-play) optical amplifiers, including the SFP+ EDFA it calls the world's first and the smallest optical amplifier available, draw interest from data center service providers and Tier-1 transmission system makers; its ultra-compact single-channel amplifier (59x16x7.5mm, 1.8W or less) is drawing interest from data-center-related system makers and is turning into sales. It also supplies self-developed DWDM amplifiers to a Japanese Tier-1 system maker. Explaining the shortfall against its 2022 merger forecasts, the company says new products such as lasers and PnP optical amplifiers entered the market 1-2 years later than expected but entered a recovery from 2025 on AI data center and defense demand, while delayed 5G investment in Japan and North America hurt amplifier and DAS sales and the digital transition of a major European customer cut RONU demand.

Customer concentration (customers above 10% of revenue, names undisclosed), H1 2026 revenue in KRW thousand: Customer A 844,888 (H1 2025: 596,929), Customer B 961,448 (1,116,502), Customer C 2,062,538 (1,806,597), Customer D 1,435,212 (535,424).
